title: SonicRoute
betaChanges: **Pair two Windows PCs.** Open Windows Link in SonicRoute Full on both PCs. Find the other PC on your local network or enter its address, then confirm the matching eight-digit code on both screens.
**Choose where audio plays.** Drag an app to the other PC to play it there or on both PCs at once. You can also send the whole system mix or select multiple outputs for one source.

**Share a window or display with sound.** Grant permission to let the other person use their keyboard and mouse. You can also transfer files and folders between PCs. Turn on clipboard sync on both PCs to share newly copied plain text.
**Browse Android files from your PC.** Select multiple files to transfer in either direction. This update also improves wireless audio and clipboard sync after idle periods or reconnection.
tagline: Send each app's audio to the device you choose.
intro: Keep music on your speakers and games or calls on your headset. SonicRoute is a Windows audio utility that lives in the system tray: choose output and input devices for individual apps, control audio with hotkeys, the tray wheel or a panel, and combine routine actions into automation rules.

downloadIntro: Choose Full x64 for optional Android phone audio, virtual-display and AirPlay integration; choose Lite x64 for PC-only audio features, Legacy x64 for .NET Framework 4.8 systems, or the experimental ARM64 editions for ARM64 PCs. Full includes optional phone and AirPlay integration; Lite and Legacy do not. Microsoft Store provides Full and Lite, and currently available versions are shown on the Store pages. Direct download links below are for {release}.
liteRequirement: Single-file portable edition; requires matching .NET 10 Desktop Runtime, PC audio features only.
legacyRequirement: No extra runtime required; relies on built-in .NET Framework 4.8, unpack and run.
storeRequirement: Full / Lite editions; requires x64 .NET 10 Desktop Runtime; Store listing controls availability.
runtimeNote: Full and Lite require {runtime}; Legacy relies on built-in .NET Framework 4.8 and needs no runtime installation (historical {runtime8} editions are discontinued).
steps: **Launch & Keep in Tray**: Double-click to start; SonicRoute stays in your system tray (drag it out of the overflow menu to keep it pinned). Double-click the tray icon to open the main window.
**Select & Route Devices**: Check your headphones and speakers under Settings → Kept devices. Left-click the tray icon to pop up the quick panel, and route each app with instant volume sliders.

**Tray Blind Control & Shortcuts**: Hover over the system tray and scroll to adjust app volume, Alt+scroll to switch audio routes, or Shift+scroll for master volume; combine with global mute hotkeys and automation for seamless in-game control.
commandNote: The `sr` command communicates with a running SonicRoute instance via named pipe in milliseconds (will not start an instance if absent). Launch SonicRoute once to register the command, then restart your terminal to integrate with scripts, AutoHotkey, or Stream Deck. If needed, refer to {faq}.

releaseSummary: v1.33 adds a self-built C# AirPlay audio and aspect-preserving screen mirror receiver to Full (PCM/ALAC/AAC-LC/AAC-ELD, optional PIN, topmost/F11 fullscreen, and drag-and-drop routing to PC or Android speakers/Bluetooth), H.265 (HEVC) with H.264 fallback, Audio/Video decoder selectors with visible-only encoder queries, foreground-gated gamepads, a combined QR (2-min auto-refresh) and manual pairing card, saved wireless LAN discovery and unified reconnect/quick-panel/sidebar refresh verification (filtering expired ports via TCP probes and recovering updated IP/port by saved device identity while preserving manual address drafts on failure), and device settings restore; across all editions (Full/Lite/Legacy), it adds two independent persistent mic OSD toggles, a single-row Configuration management card, >20-row app list virtualization, coalesced OSD rendering, PNG input and retired texture release, removal of explicit close-window GC requests in Full (leaving collection to the runtime), config .bak protection, on-demand error diagnostics, standalone Store Lite support, and an offline GPL-3.0-only viewer. features: **Independent app audio routing (playback + recording).** Assign output and input devices to individual apps—send games and voice chat to headphones and headsets, and music to speakers. Settings persist natively in Windows even after closing SonicRoute, without altering system mixer settings.

**Smart foreground focus and tray wheel blind adjustments.** System events lock onto the active audio app in milliseconds. Scroll directly over the system tray to adjust volume or Alt+scroll to switch devices, paired with on-screen OSD feedback and global mic mute, without leaving your active window.
**Quick panel and live audio activity indicators.** The card panel features 350–850px adjustable height and position saving; control per-app volume sliders with real-time sound activity meters.

**Android Phone Integration & AirPlay Reception (Full Edition)**: Route Android audio into PC with per-app volume and adaptive virtual display windows (with H.265 and foreground gamepad support) or stream PC audio to phone; receive Apple AirPlay audio and aspect-preserving screen mirroring directly in C#, route AirPlay to PC outputs or connected Android speakers/Bluetooth from Quick Panel, and balance loudness with SmartVolume.

**Automation combo engine and blazing CLI (6 triggers × 39 actions).** Trigger rules by app launch, focus, exit, schedule, hotkeys, or startup. Chain device switching, volume, muting, app launch with file associations, and PowerShell scripts; use the built-in sr named-pipe command for instant script and hardware deck control without extra background processes.

**Event-first detection.** Uses system notifications with a necessary one-second snapshot fallback when needed, and cleans up unneeded data on demand. Full adds optional Android phone audio, virtual-display and AirPlay integration; Lite and Legacy remain PC-only. Available in nine languages.

faqQuestions: Will app routing and volume settings persist after closing SonicRoute?
Which runtime does each edition require?
Does running SonicRoute in the background consume CPU or battery?
faqAnswers: Windows keeps app routes and existing audio sessions after SonicRoute closes. Hotkeys, tray controls, automation, phone audio, screen mirroring and clipboard sync require SonicRoute to keep running.

Full and Lite require the matching .NET 10 Desktop Runtime; Legacy uses .NET Framework 4.8. The Store package needs the x64 .NET 10 Desktop Runtime. Historical NET8 builds are no longer maintained, but archived downloads remain available.
Detection prioritizes system events and uses a necessary one-second snapshot fallback when needed. Unneeded data is cleaned up on demand; actual CPU use depends on the system and workload.
